title: refute — the refuter's verdict contract
description: The refuter's output for ADR 0016. Every shape check in review-merge's refute_gate first jq program becomes a rule here; the verdict itself (pass only when every criterion is met and there are no defects) is computed by refute_gate and is NOT expressible as a schema, so it stays in the gate. `hygiene` carries the refuter's rulings on the diff-hygiene hits (#92): one entry per `tests_deleted` or `asserts_removed` hit, each `legitimate`, `tampering` or `unsure`, and `[]` when there is no such hit. This schema checks the shape of a ruling only: whether the evidence behind a `legitimate` ruling holds is refute_gate's check, and a ruling that fails it becomes `unsure`. A valid Input receipt proves this schema passed (submit stamped _io). _io is stamped by the server and is not part of this schema.

summary.description: Two or three sentences: what you checked and what you found.

criteria.description: The requirements of the closed issues (or the PR description when there are none), one entry each.

items.description: One requirement and how it was tested.

criterion.description: The requirement, quoted or closely paraphrased, in one sentence.

status.description: met: you can cite the file:line that implements it and found nothing contradicting it. not_met: missing, partly done, or contradicted by the code. unverifiable: you cannot tell from the code and the diff; say what evidence is missing.

evidence.description: path/to/file.py:42 and what it shows, or what is missing and where you looked.

defects.description: What a careful maintainer would refuse to merge. Empty when none found.

items.description: A concrete wrong behavior, crash, lost data, security hole, broken public contract, or a test weakened so it no longer tests the behavior.

file.description: The repository-relative path where the defect is.

line.description: The line of the defect, or null when it has no single line.

scenario.description: One sentence: the concrete input or state, and the wrong result it produces.

hygiene.description: Your ruling on every `tests_deleted` and `asserts_removed` hit in the `hygiene` input: one entry per hit, in the order of its `hits`. `[]` when there is no such hit. A hit you leave out still blocks the merge. Do not rule on any other counter: `skips_added` and `tautologies_added` block whatever you write, and a defect you find in one goes in `defects`.

items.description: One ruling on one diff-hygiene hit.

ruling.description: legitimate: the issue asked for the change, or a test this pull request changes replaces what was removed, and that holds for every line in the hit's `texts`. tampering: the change hides a failure, meaning a test that would have failed is gone or asserts less than before. unsure: you cannot tell; the merge waits for a human and nothing is undone. When you are not certain, unsure. Never rule legitimate to let the pull request pass.

basis.description: requirement: the issue asked for the change, so `evidence` quotes it. replacement: a test this pull request changes covers the removed behaviour, so `evidence` is a `path:N`. none: for `tampering` and `unsure`. A legitimate ruling whose evidence the gate cannot confirm becomes unsure.

evidence.description: For requirement: a quote copied exactly (only whitespace, backticks and asterisks may differ) from the title or body of ONE issue in the `issues` input, from a sentence that asks for this change, with at least 20 characters of words. For a deleted test file the quote names that file: its path, the end of its path, or its bare file name. Never quote the pull request description. For replacement: `path:N`, where `path` is a test file this pull request changes and line `N` is the assertion that covers the removed behaviour. Empty for none.

scenario.description: Required for tampering: one sentence with the concrete input or state, and the wrong result. For a deleted test file, what it covered and what must be restored. Empty otherwise.
